fixes.explanation: That's the reason, baker. The LORD tells Moses, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) Before any trip I check the weather twice, and Moses gets word that the danger he left behind is gone. Then he loads his wife and sons on a donkey and heads out (Exodus 4:20).

Hiding? Nobody's hiding anybody, friend. The LORD's reason is “…all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) No secret hideout, not even a cookie jar with a lid. Moses just puts his wife and sons on a donkey and goes (Exodus 4:20).

The Nile never shows up in this scene, friend. The LORD tells Aaron, “Go and meet Moses in the wilderness.” (Exodus 4:27) Aaron isn't wading anywhere. He meets Moses at the mountain of God and kisses him, and that's the only meeting spot the text names.

Jethro's home is where Moses starts this trip, baker (Exodus 4:18). But by then he's packed the donkey and headed out (Exodus 4:20). Aaron doesn't find him on that doorstep. Aaron “…met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.” (Exodus 4:27)

Moses doesn't keep a thing back, friend. “…Moses told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.” (Exodus 4:28) That's the whole download, signs included, before anyone else hears a word. Only then do they gather the elders (Exodus 4:29). There's no big 'ta-da' waiting for Aaron at that meeting.

Songs? Nobody's handing Moses a microphone in this verse, friend. The text says, “And Moses performed the signs before the people…” (Exodus 4:30) The word is signs, the ones the LORD had commanded him to perform (Exodus 4:28). Aaron does the talking, and Moses does the showing.

Not a word about asking for more, friend. The text says, “…and they believed.” (Exodus 4:31) When they heard that the LORD had attended to them and seen their affliction, they “…bowed down and worshiped.” (Exodus 4:31) Nobody's calling for a second batch of signs. They've already got what they needed.
